title: Lesson 1: Nikhilam — Multiply Near Base 100
subtopics: Multiply deficits to get right part
learningGoals: Understand the concept of a deficit as distance from the base 100.
Apply the Nikhilam sutra to multiply two numbers both close to 100.
Extend the method to cases where one number is above 100.
coreIdeas: Find how far each number is from 100 — those are the deficits.
Cross-subtract: take either number minus the other's deficit.
Multiply the two deficits together for the right-hand part.
Concatenate left part | right part (pad right part to 2 digits if needed).

workedExamples.method: Deficits: 100−97=3, 100−96=4. Cross: 97−4=93 (or 96−3=93). Product of deficits: 3×4=12. Answer: 93|12 = 9312.

onboarding.coachIntro: Hi! I am Arya, your Vedic Maths coach. Today you will learn to multiply numbers near 100 — like 97×96 — in just three steps. No long multiplication needed!
onboarding.placementRule: If learner knows what a deficit is, skip Group A and start at Group B.

mission.missionPromise: Master the Nikhilam sutra and multiply 2-digit numbers near 100 at lightning speed.
mission.successCelebration: Incredible! You have cracked the Nikhilam code. Large multiplications feel tiny now!

microLessonPattern: Arya names the sutra and shows one punchy example.
Board highlights both numbers and their distances from 100.
Student identifies the deficit before attempting the full product.
Instant feedback zooms in on which part (left or right) needs attention.
Review prompt asks student to verbally state the two steps.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise C: Cross-subtract for the left part
sessionFlow.coachHook: Step 2 — cross-subtract! Take the first number and subtract the SECOND number's deficit. Or the other way — both give the same result!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 97×96: deficit of 96 is 4. So 97−4 = 93. Also 96−3 = 93. Left part = 93!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Cross-subtraction nailed! Left part locked in.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Left part = first number − deficit of second. For 94×93: 94−7 = 87.

exercises.hint: Subtract the second number's deficit from the first number.

sessionFlow.subtopic: Multiply deficits to get right part
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Multiply deficits for the right part
sessionFlow.coachHook: Step 3 — multiply the two deficits! For 97×96: deficits are 3 and 4. So 3×4=12. That is the RIGHT part!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 97×96: deficits 3 and 4. Right part = 3×4 = 12. If right part is a single digit, pad with a zero on the left!
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: For 98×95 (deficits 2,5): what is the right part?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Right part correct! Remember to pad to 2 digits if needed.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Right part = deficit1 × deficit2. For 99×97: 1×3=3 → pad to 03.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What is the right part for 95×92?

exercises.questionText: For 99 × 97, deficits are 1 and 3. The right part (padded to 2 digits) is:
exercises.solution: 1 × 3 = 3. Since it is a single digit, pad to 03.
